holidays.name: Balloon Ascension Day
holidays.description: A day to look up and celebrate the dreamy, drifting wonder of ballooning. It honors the moment humans first floated into the sky beneath a big bubble of air.
holidays.origin: The day marks January 9, 1793. On that day French aeronaut Jean-Pierre Blanchard made the first hot-air-style balloon flight in North America. He took off from Philadelphia, and President George Washington was among the spectators.
holidays.funFact: Blanchard carried a passport signed by Washington. It was meant to help him if he landed somewhere unexpected, and he did land in a New Jersey field.

holidays.name: National Apricot Day
holidays.description: A day for savoring the small, golden, velvety fruit. Eat them fresh, bake them into tarts, or stir them into jam.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance, and its origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Apricots are close relatives of plums and peaches, and their kernels are used to flavor amaretto-style treats.

holidays.name: National Static Electricity Day
holidays.description: A shocking celebration of the zaps, crackles and hair-raising moments that come with static electricity. Rub a balloon on your head and enjoy the show.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is usually celebrated in the dry depths of winter, when static is at its peak.
holidays.funFact: A static spark that you can feel can carry thousands of volts. The energy is so tiny that it is harmless.
